macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks fall sharply as AI shares sell off
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 1.09%, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.14%, and the Dow declined 0.34% in Friday trading. Semiconductor and other AI-linked stocks led the selloff as investors questioned whether massive AI infrastructure spending will generate adequate returns.

items.title: Fed officials offer no clear signal before October meeting
items.summary: Federal Reserve officials expressed concern about persistent inflation, with Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee warning that strong AI data-center demand could add to price pressures. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh gave no indication of whether rates would change at the October 27–28 meeting, while the central bank entered its pre-meeting communications blackout.

items.title: Treasury yields and volatility rise as markets retreat
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield was reported near 5.08%, while the S&P 500 volatility index rose more than 21% to 19.99. Higher borrowing costs and geopolitical risks added to pressure on equities.

items.title: Major technology and corporate earnings set to dominate the week ahead
items.summary: Investors are preparing for results from Tesla, Meta Platforms, IBM, General Motors and other major companies. Analysts expect technology and AI-related earnings to provide key signals about corporate profitability and the sustainability of AI investment.

items.title: European shares recover modestly as technology stocks gain
items.summary: European equities rose modestly, helped by technology shares and strong demand reported by ASML. Investors continued to monitor elevated energy prices, geopolitical tensions and upcoming inflation data for clues about central-bank policy.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin trades near $81,600 after volatile session
items.summary: Bitcoin was reported near $81,600 as buyers attempted to stabilize the market following recent volatility. Other market reports placed BTC around $81,250, up 1.21% over 24 hours, while BNB was down 1.55%.[1][2]

items.title: Digital-asset investment products see $434 million weekly outflow
items.summary: CoinShares reported $434 million in net outflows from digital-asset investment products during the week, with stronger-than-expected U.S. inflation cited among the market pressures.[3]

items.title: Deutsche Bank plans institutional crypto custody service
items.summary: Deutsche Bank reportedly plans to launch a cryptocurrency custody service within weeks, initially supporting Bitcoin and Ethereum and targeting professional clients in Germany.[3][4]

items.title: DTCC launches tokenization service
items.summary: The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation reportedly launched a tokenization service whose initial assets represent approximately $30 trillion in securities.[3]

items.title: Charles Schwab expands direct Bitcoin and Ethereum access
items.summary: Charles Schwab reportedly made direct cryptocurrency purchases available through customer accounts, covering more than 40 million U.S. users, with New York and Louisiana residents excluded initially.[5]

items.title: Polygon Labs completes Coinme acquisition
items.summary: Polygon Labs reportedly completed its acquisition of Coinme as part of an effort to expand into stablecoin infrastructure and payments.[4]

items.title: NEAR reports $3.8 million smart-contract exploit
items.summary: NEAR Intents disclosed a security incident in which an interaction and refund flaw produced approximately $3.8 million in fraudulent balances across 23 failed deposit transactions before funds were extracted through cross-chain infrastructure.[5]

items.title: Celestia leads weekly altcoin gains
items.summary: Celestia’s TIA token rose 57% over the week to about $0.75, its highest level since November 2025, following the launch of Eden, an EVM-compatible chain for AI-agent experimentation.[6]

items.title: Bitcoin mining difficulty rises 5.92%
items.summary: Bitcoin’s mining difficulty reportedly increased 5.92% to 140.58T, following a previous adjustment that was nearly unchanged.[5]

items.title: Dormant Bitcoin wallets move 416.69 BTC
items.summary: Two Bitcoin wallets inactive for more than 12 years reportedly transferred approximately 416.69 BTC, with unrealized gains estimated at $33.71 million.[7]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: DeepSeek releases faster, leaner V4.1-Flash-1017 model
items.summary: DeepSeek released an updated AI model for its web service, app, and developer platform, claiming stronger reasoning, coding, agentic-task, and visual-benchmark performance with faster task completion and shorter outputs. The launch intensifies competition between Chinese open-weight models and proprietary U.S. systems.

items.title: Google DeepMind reports high Gemini 4 Argon benchmark score
items.summary: Google DeepMind’s Gemini 4 Argon reportedly scored 97.5% on ARC-AGI-3, though its result fell to 49.8% under the benchmark’s standard test harness. The model is also being rolled out across developer, enterprise, subscriber, and coding-tool products.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly unveils Claude Sonnet 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic announced Claude Sonnet 5.5 as a faster and cheaper mid-tier model, with claims of more than 30% higher speed and up to 30% lower cost for typical work. The model reportedly powers Claude’s free tier.

items.title: Google DeepMind open-sources AlphaProtein Novo
items.summary: Google DeepMind reportedly released AlphaProtein Novo, an AI system designed to create novel enzymes from scratch for targeted chemical-production tasks. The development highlights the expansion of generative AI into protein and biotechnology research.

items.title: ByteDance launches OmniHuman 2.0 video model
items.summary: ByteDance released OmniHuman 2.0 through BytePlus, with the model generating videos from a single image and audio track for durations of up to five minutes. The company says costs have fallen 40%, with API pricing reported at $0.07 per second.

items.title: CERN and Mistral plan large physics model
items.summary: CERN and Mistral signed a statement of intent to build a foundation model for collider physics, trained on simulated Large Hadron Collider data. The system is intended to assist with particle reconstruction and identification.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox launches Xbox Labs to bring games to web browsers
items.summary: Microsoft announced Xbox Labs, a small engineering unit exploring ways to make older-generation games playable in web browsers and expand game distribution across devices.

items.title: Epic reportedly delays Disney and Marvel shooter amid AI development push
items.summary: Epic Games has reportedly delayed its unannounced Disney-related Marvel and Star Wars shooter indefinitely while directing developers toward fully AI-generated art workflows.

items.title: Indie game demo canceled over AI cloning concerns
items.summary: The developers of Drunken Goddess Reflux canceled a public demo because they feared the game’s distinctive concept could be copied using AI tools. Testing will instead take place in closed sessions.

items.title: US bill seeks permanent ownership protections for digital games
items.summary: Representative Ritchie Torres is preparing legislation that would strengthen consumer ownership rights for purchased games, including protections against games disappearing from digital storefronts or becoming inaccessible after server closures.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign launches early for some players
items.summary: Activision released the campaign for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 to pre-order customers, with DMZ scheduled for October 20 and the full release set for October 23.

items.title: GTA 6 PC version reportedly planned for early 2027
items.summary: Industry sources reportedly indicate that Grand Theft Auto VI will launch on PC during the first quarter of 2027, several months after its planned November 19, 2026 release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

items.title: Steam Next Fest to feature ArcheAge Chronicles demo
items.summary: Valve’s upcoming Steam Next Fest will run from October 20 to October 27, with XL Games planning to release a free worldwide demo of the open-world MMORPG ArcheAge Chronicles.

items.title: Kwalee lays off Luna Abyss development team
items.summary: Publisher Kwalee reportedly laid off the entire development team behind Luna Abyss shortly after the shooter’s release and positive critical reception.
